examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Pick any number of options. The picks show as chips in the field. Keep them in state and update them from `onValueChange`, which receives the full list of values.

examples.title: Uncontrolled
examples.description: Use `defaultValue` for the starting picks when you only need to hear about changes.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: `value` is the source of truth, so anything can change it: here a button picks every option.

examples.title: Searchable
examples.description: `searchable` adds a search field to the list and focuses it on open (on a mouse, not on touch). Search matches the label, the caption and the group name.

examples.title: Groups
examples.description: Pass sections instead of a flat list: `{ label, options }`. Group names head each block and are searchable too.

examples.title: Select all
examples.description: `selectAllLabel` pins a row at the top that picks every enabled option, shows a dash for a partial selection and clears when everything is picked.

examples.title: Selection limit
examples.description: `maxSelections` stops further picks and dims the rest. The footer counts them; hide it with `showSelectionFooter={false}`.

examples.title: Detailed rows
examples.description: `optionVariant="detailed"` puts a checkbox in front of each row and shows `caption` on the right, for people, lines or numbers that need a second line of context.

examples.title: Chip limit
examples.description: `maxVisible` keeps the field one line high: the chips past the limit become a "+N" count (hover it to read them). Without it, chips wrap and the field grows a row every few picks.

examples.title: Summary
examples.description: `summaryLabel` swaps the chips for one line of text, such as "3 lines selected". Hover it to read the picks.

examples.title: Disabled options
examples.description: A disabled option cannot be picked and is skipped by the arrow keys. `disabledTooltip` says why on hover.

examples.title: Helper text and error
examples.description: `helperText` sits under the field and `error` replaces it in red. The row opens smoothly, and both are linked to the field for assistive technology.

examples.title: Loading and paging
examples.description: `loading` shows a spinner while the first page is fetched. `onScrollEnd`, `hasMore` and `loadingMore` page more options in as the list is scrolled.

examples.title: Server-side search
examples.description: Set `searchQuery` and `onSearchQueryChange` and the field stops filtering for itself: you pass the options that match. Picked values that are not in the current results still show as chips.

examples.title: Inside a dialog
examples.description: The list is portaled to the page, so a dialog does not clip it, and it keeps working with the dialog's focus trap. Escape closes the list first and the dialog second.

examples.title: In a form
examples.description: `name` submits one entry per pick, so a plain form post or `FormData` reads them with `getAll`.

examples.title: Keyboard
examples.description: The field is a combobox: arrows move through the rows, typing jumps to a match, Escape returns to the field and Backspace drops the last pick.
